title: AZ affinity congestion + kubelet throttle — oncall walkthrough
body:
Summary:
During the 2026-03-04 morning deploy window we observed a large, regional scheduling slowdown in us-west-2 caused by an interaction of AZ-affinity constraints, CNI conntrack growth, and kubelet CPU stalls when processing container runtime I/O. Symptoms presented as a wave of pods stuck in Pending for 30–90s each (p95 scheduling latency jumped to ~45s), high API-server write latencies, and occasional node-level OOM kill spikes on the offending node pool.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture on-call diagnostics for the immediate mitigation decisions we made.
- Record root cause hypotheses and confidence levels.
- List short-term mitigations and concrete follow-ups (tickets + owners) to prevent recurrence.

Systems impacted:
- Kube-scheduler (scheduling latency p95 up from 0.8s -> ~45s)
- Application pods in green and blue pools with topologySpread/affinity by az label
- CNI (Calico) conntrack tables on nodes in az-a and az-b pools
- Node kubelet / containerd on some GPU and CPU nodes (kubelet threads stuck)

High-level timeline (local times):
- 08:05: deploy started (canary + ramp)
- 08:12: first pager: pod create/create-sandboxes timing out in region us-west-2 (Slack channel #sre-incidents)
- 08:18: observed cluster-wide Pending spike; scheduler P90->P95 moved sharply
- 08:25: focused on az-a pool nodes showing high conntrack counts and elevated SYN_RECV counts
- 08:30: scaled up new nodes in az-c to relieve pressure and temporarily disabled strict AZ affinity for one rollout group
- 08:42: scheduler latency began to recover after conntrack sysctl bump and rolling drain of the most affected nodes
- 09:10: incident declared mitigated; continued monitoring until 11:00

Key observations and metrics at peak:
- p95 scheduling latency: ~45s (baseline ~0.8s)
- API server write latency p95: increased from 30ms -> 300ms under load
- Conntrack table utilization on az-a nodes: 210k entries (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max was 262144)
- Long tail of conntrack TIME_WAIT and ESTABLISHED sockets to external services (sidecar egress patterns)
- Top processes consuming CPU during stalls: kubelet showing frequent goroutine stacks in snapshotter layer, containerd snapshotter io wait spikes
- Node memory: transient page cache growth then some OOMs for user processes after heavy churn

Signals that mattered (queries we ran):
- conntrack counts: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l (or /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count)
- kernel socket states per node: ss -s and ss -tan | awk '{print $1,$2,$3}' | sort -n
- kubelet stacks: curl -s localhost:10248/metrics | grep goroutines and journalctl -u kubelet -n 500
- scheduler profiling: kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/kube-scheduler -c kube-scheduler --since=1h | grep "scheduling latency"
- API server latency: graph panels in Grafana (apiserver_request_duration_seconds)

Immediate mitigations applied (chronological):
1) Emergency scaling: spun up 25% additional nodes in az-c to redistribute pending pods off saturated az-a/az-b pools. (Command: terraform apply -var='node_pool=az-c-burst')
2) Affinity relax: for the active rollout group we temporarily removed strict topologySpreadAffinity rules by pushing a short-lived override to the rollout controller so new pods could schedule anywhere. (PR: github.com/redwood/rollouts/pull/1893 — emergency revert enqueued)
3) Conntrack tuning: increased nf_conntrack_max on half the affected nodes from 262144 -> 524288 and lowered nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait to reduce TIME_WAIT tail. (sysctl commands below). Rollout via SSM runbook for consistent change.
4) Node rotation: drained and rebooted the 6 worst nodes (highest conntrack + kernel socket backlog). Draining helped free up per-node resources and cleared transient containerd snapshot locks.
5) API server rate-limiting check: confirmed no runaway client causing API pressure (none found). Rate limits and admission controller remained healthy.

Commands used (copyable):
- Check conntrack: cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
- Increase conntrack max: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
- Shorten TIME_WAIT: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=30
- Find top socket states: ss -tna | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
- Kubelet dump: curl -sS localhost:10248/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2 > /tmp/kubelet-goroutines-$(hostname)
- Drain node: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force

Root cause analysis (hypotheses, confidence):
A) Primary: AZ-affinity + uneven AZ utilization produced concentrated churn on az-a/az-b nodepools during rollout. Many pods had topologySpread/Affinity that pinned them to limited AZ capacity. This caused higher connection churn per-node (confident, ~75%).
B) Secondary: CNI/host conntrack exhaustion magnified scheduler latency because kubelet/containerd evictions and network stalls made pod sandbox creation slow; connections to external dependencies stayed in TIME_WAIT leading to growth (moderate confidence, ~60%).
C) Contributing: containerd snapshotter I/O stalls and kubelet goroutine contention (low-to-moderate confidence, ~50%). We saw stack traces pointing at snapshotter wait and heavy lock contention during the spike.

Why scheduler latency increases when conntrack high:
- Kubelet spends longer creating sandboxes and reporting NodeStatus; scheduler's cache becomes stale and some admission paths block on API server responses leading to longer schedule cycles. Also, probe latencies for readiness/liveness cause more churn.

Follow-ups and owners (short-ticket list):
- SRE-1428 (owner: Ethan McCoy): Remove unsafe strict AZ affinity in rollout templates and add fallback rules for low-capacity AZs (duedate 2026-03-20)
- SRE-1429 (owner: Lina Gomez): Investigate and harden conntrack observability and autoscaling: add per-node conntrack alert and auto-scaler action to avoid hitting 80% (duedate 2026-03-12)
- SRE-1430 (owner: Tomas Rivera): Audit sidecar egress patterns (circuit breakers) to reduce extraneous short-lived TCP connections (duedate 2026-03-25)
- SRE-1431 (owner: Priya Nair): Add kubelet snapshotter and containerd p99 CPU/IO dashboards and correlate with scheduling latency (duedate 2026-03-15)
- SRE-1432 (owner: Platform Eng): Kernel tuning baseline proposal (conntrack defaults, timeouts) for region-specific profiles (duedate 2026-04-01)

Longer term mitigation candidates (discussion items):
- Add topology-aware autoscaler that respects AZ imbalance and proactively rebalances before rollout (requires scheduler + autoscaler changes)
- Implement conntrack autosizing via node-level controller that increases nf_conntrack_max when short on headroom (safety concerns: kernel memory consumption)
- Replace sidecar egress patterns with pooled HTTP/GRPC connection pools to reduce ephemeral TCP churn
- Improve rollout controller to detect AZ saturation and reduce rollout parallelism for AZ-constrained services

Open questions and unknowns:
- Why did containerd snapshotter stall coincide exactly with conntrack growth? Are there kernel I/O scheduling interactions that amplify socket table pressure? (need deeper kernel tracing)
- Should we change deployment templates to prefer anti-affinity across AZs rather than strict affinity? Impacts to latency and data locality need benchmarking.
- Are there particular services that create the majority of short-lived connections? (initial sampling suggests sidecars for logging and metrics but needs more concrete evidence)

Notes for runbook improvements (quick wins):
- Add explicit conntrack-check step in the node health playbook with automated remediation suggestions (increase limit + drain)
- Add a scheduler-liveness panel to our oncall dashboard to highlight p95 scheduling latency + queued pods per nodepool
- Add an emergency affordance in the rollout controller to relax topologySpreadAffinity on detection of scheduling p95 > 20s for >2 minutes

Appendix (logs/snippets):
- Example conntrack tail (node az-a-12): 212341 entries, states: TIME_WAIT 170k, ESTABLISHED 20k, SYN_RECV 18k
- kubelet goroutine snapshot (truncated):
  goroutine 11245 [semacquire, 120 minutes]:
    sync.runtime_SemacquireMutex
    k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/someSnapshotWait
    k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime.(*GenericRuntimeManager).StartContainer

- Slack notes: incident runbook triggered by Ethan at 08:15; decision to bump conntrack made after 08:28 kernel counts review.

If you were oncall next shift:
1) Review SRE-1429 and ensure per-node conntrack alert has a sane threshold (80% of nf_conntrack_max) and a playbook for safe sysctl changes.
2) Make sure the emergency rollback PR for the affinity override is staged and documented (PR link in linked_artifacts).
3) Coordinate with platform to run a controlled experiment with conntrack_max bumps on a canary node pool to measure memory impact.

End of notes.
